description: Four-option run — the shape that produced ROADMAP 1.121, where the enricher emitted four review_cards ALL titled "A load-bearing assumption", colliding on dedupe and giving the canvas nothing to focus. story_headlines is the source field for those titles, so the defect is measurable here.

provenance.note: The only fixture with more than two options, so it is also the only one where headline collision is POSSIBLE — the distinctness dimension reports "collision impossible" everywhere else and says so rather than claiming a pass it did not earn.

input.brief: Which of our four growth bets should get next quarter budget?

candidates.label: good
candidates.note: Four distinct, option-specific headlines. Should PASS.

output.narrative_summary: Self Serve Funnel comes out ahead by about 14 percentage points over Paid Acquisition. Customer acquisition cost is the input that moves all four bets.

story_headlines.opt_selfserve: Ahead because acquisition cost bites it least
story_headlines.opt_paid: Close behind, most exposed to acquisition cost
story_headlines.opt_partner: Middling return with a narrow spread

robustness_explanation.summary: The ordering holds in about 64% of runs, with acquisition cost driving most of the movement.
robustness_explanation.primary_risk: Customer acquisition cost could rise and compress every bet at once.
fragility_factors: Customer acquisition cost reverses the ordering in about 33% of runs.

output.readiness_rationale: The ordering is usable, but customer acquisition cost moves all four bets together, so it should be watched.

fac_cac.why: Customer acquisition cost is the single input shaping every bet.
fac_cac.expected_gain: Would firm up all four at once.

edge_cac_growth.context: If customer acquisition cost rises, new revenue falls across every bet and the ordering tightens.

key_assumptions: Customer acquisition cost stays inside the range examined.

decision_quality_prompts.prompt: What would have to happen to customer acquisition cost for the ordering to change?
